title: Chronological Audit Reconciliation Protocol for External Sinks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Third-party sinks (Splunk, Datadog, custom webhooks) ingest audit events from Redwood. Customers require a contract that guarantees chronological reconciliation across tenant-scoped streams while preserving at-least-once durability and practical ordering guarantees for downstream SIEMs. Current behavior: events can be duplicated, reordered during spikes, and DLQ handling is inconsistent across sinks. This ticket defines a protocol and implementation plan for: 1) embedding low-overhead reconciliation metadata into audit envelopes, 2) durable transient staging with per-tenant monotonic sequence watermarks, 3) a sink contract for ack semantics and backpressure, and 4) operational tooling (metrics, dashboards, and replay helpers) for reconstructing chronological order in tenant-scoped views.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope includes immutable fields: tenant_id, monotonic_seq (64-bit), event_id (uuid v4), schema_version, prev_seq_signature
Per-tenant staging queue persists events until acknowledged by downstream or moved to DLQ after configurable retry window
At-least-once delivery with idempotency support: sinks can dedupe by event_id and seq window
Reconciliation tool can reconstruct a strict chronological stream for a tenant given ingested events and staging state within 5 minutes on a 24-hour retention window
SLA: 99.95% of events acknowledged by primary sink within 30s under normal load; fallback to secondary sink within 60s on primary failures
Automated integration tests against mock Splunk and Datadog endpoints that assert ordering under concurrent writes and simulated restarts
Documentation: Public contract page (Confluence) and SDK snippet for building idempotent sink consumers
Security: All audit envelopes signed with per-tenant HMAC and encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest in staging
implementation_notes: Add monotonic_seq: use per-tenant sequence allocator service backed by Redis or Raft leader to avoid clock-based ordering
Attach prev_seq_signature: small HMAC over previous seq to make sequence forks detectable during reconciliation
Staging store: use existing audit-forwarder topic with ordered partitions by tenant hash and durable retention; implement transactional write/commit semantics
Backpressure model: honor sink 429/503 with exponential backoff, but surface tenant-level token bucket metrics to decide adaptive throttling
DLQ policy: move to DLQ after N attempts or after age threshold; include hints for automated replay (time windows, seq ranges)
Idempotency: recommend sinks dedupe by event_id and track last_applied_seq per tenant; provide SDK helper that manages small LRU state and checkpointing
Contract for sinks: accept events with header X-Redwood-Audit-Version and return JSON ack {status: 'ok', last_seq_applied: <seq>} or standard HTTP error codes
Fallback: if primary sink reports inconsistent seq (gap or fork), forwarder marks tenant as 'reconcile-needed' and triggers incremental replay to reconcile state
Performance: batch events where possible but maintain batch order; default max batch size 128 events or 256KB whichever first
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable protocol on 5 low-traffic tenants and route to mock Splunk/Datadog endpoints; collect metrics
Phase 2 (pilot): opt-in for 20 customers, enable staging store retention=48h, enable reconciliation tooling
Phase 3 (gradual): enable by default for new tenants; provide migration script for existing tenants to backfill seqs
Phase 4 (enforcement): require sinks to implement ack contract; deprecate legacy webhook mode after 8 weeks
Communication: notify customers via admin console banner and changelog; provide SDK and migration guide
test_plan: Unit tests for sequence allocator and HMAC signing/verification
Integration tests with a Splunk HTTP Event Collector mock that simulates partial acks and delays
Chaos test: force forwarder restarts and network partitions to validate at-least-once and DLQ behavior
Load test: 10k events/s across 1k tenants to verify staging latency and max backlog sizing
End-to-end: reconciliation tool proves monotonic reconstructed stream equals original order in 99.99% of runs under test conditions
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: per-tenant lag_seconds between event produced and last_seq_applied reported by sink
Metric: staging_queue_depth per partition and global
Alert: tenant_reconcile_needed if gap_detected > 1 minute or if DLQ rate exceeds threshold
SLO dashboard: percent of events delivered within 30s (target 99.95%), percent of successfully reconciled tenants
Runbook link for oncall: steps to force replay, escalate to engineering, and notify customer support
